source_locator.passage_anchor: The seventh house represents the Physician
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: The seventh house represents the physician and the tenth his medicine. If the seventh lord is unfortunate, the physician shall not cure. For the tenth house or its ruler the printed phrase 'his Physick is improper' does not repeat an explicit affliction verb; the adverse qualifier must not be silently supplied as an exact quote.
prerequisites: Medical horary figure.
Assess separately the seventh-ruler state and tenth-house/tenth-ruler state.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Provider, medicine and patient significators are distinct.
Failure and treatment appropriateness are claims of the historical text, not evidence.
The tenth-house clause has a missing explicit verb/predicate; 'be unfortunate' is a plausible but UNSUPPLIED parallel inference from the seventh-house statement.

source_locator.passage_anchor: The fourth house signifies the end of the sicknesse
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: The fourth house signifies whether sickness will end quickly or endure long; fixed signs prolong, common signs vary disease, and moveable signs 'shew an end one way or other quickly'. It does not say movable signs merely 'change' the disease.
prerequisites: Judge end or duration of sickness.
exceptions_and_modifiers: The source says the movable ending may occur one way or another, not invariably recovery.
Do not convert sign classes to exact calendar duration.

Aphorism30 says movable signs vary; #4 in a fourth-house context says movable signs end quickly. The conflict is on movable signs if applied to the same chart position; common and fixed clauses are broadly compatible.

source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: If the physician FIRST visits in Saturn's hour, 'his Patient shall either be long sick, or long in curing, and suffers much torment in his cure'; the patient is the most natural continuing subject, though the later pronoun is not fully settled. The patient is said not to be cured until almost both physician and patient despair.
prerequisites: Planetary hour at FIRST physician visit is Saturn's.
exceptions_and_modifiers: The text offers long illness OR long cure, not both necessarily.
No verified physician-patient outcomes or causal evidence.
Patient is the clear subject of long sick or long curing; the subsequent suffers torment pronoun may continue patient or shift to physician and is kept unresolved.

source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: When urine is brought, the source directs: let the ascendant represent the sick party whether the querent came with consent or not. The printed rationale says 'for the Urine was sometimes of the essence of the sick', with 'sometimes' retaining possible formerly-versus-occasionally senses.
prerequisites: A urine specimen has been brought to the physician.
exceptions_and_modifiers: No medical diagnostic validity of urine-as-essence is established.
This is the local exception to questioner-signification, not permission to ignore consent in real care.
Sometimes of the essence may mean formerly in period English or occasionally; neither sense is imposed without further collation.
Aphorism9 overlaps this case ONLY under its disjunctive missing-one reading. Under a neither-present reading #9 does not describe urine-present/no-consent. Unresolved.

source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

For a man asking about his servant (a master/servant example), sixth signifies the servant and sixth from sixth (the eleventh) the sickness; source closes '& sic in aliis, where no consent is'. This may overlap #8 when urine arrives without consent.
prerequisites: The original prints no urine OR consent, a grammatically ambiguous combination; preserve the 'or' rather than silently requiring both absent.
The questioner is distinct from the patient.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Keep derived sixth-from-sixth = eleventh and relation-specific house assignment.
This item begins on PDF316 and continues on PDF317.
Do not treat historical lack-of-consent procedure as an acceptable modern medical practice.

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Moone is more afflicted of Mars
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: The Moon increased in light is said to be more afflicted by Mars, and in her wane more oppressed by Saturn. 'Beware in the beginning of a sicknesse' when the Moon is thus unfortunated. Mars does more mischief in masculine signs, Oriental and above Earth; whether those are jointly necessary or individually aggravating is unresolved. The source asks for the contrary judgment of Saturn without spelling out all logical negations.
prerequisites: GENERAL: waxing Moon said more afflicted by Mars, waning Moon more oppressed by Saturn.
AT SICKNESS ONSET ONLY: the source urges 'beware in the beginning of a sicknesse' when the Moon is so unfortunated.
Mars being in masculine signs, oriental and above Earth are printed modifiers; joint necessity versus individually aggravating factors remains unsettled.
exceptions_and_modifiers: The Saturn converse is not a fully enumerated complementary Boolean rule in the source.
Avoid conflating waxing with speed or motion.
This is the last physician aphorism before Chapter XLV, which has a separate dated worked chart.
Record the separate sickness-onset warning; do not extend it as a necessary precondition for the general waxing/waning or Mars claims. Do not turn Mars modifiers into a compulsory conjunction.
